outcome: Create, update, standardize, import, validate, and evaluate an agent skill package without losing its use-case behavior.

audience.basis: The main agent skill package is consumed by an invoking agent. Human authors, reviewers and recipients of reports retain their distinct evidence and authority roles.

motivations.constraint: Map every package primitive to the agent skill use case.
motivations.reason: A valid skill package must help an executor produce the intended domain result.
motivations.failure_prevented: Polished agent skill boilerplate that passes shape checks but adds no domain capability.

motivations.constraint: Keep repeatable package mechanics behind the Mise task graph.
motivations.reason: Agent skill judgment works better when deterministic work has one tested path.
motivations.failure_prevented: Conflicting skill package commands and unproved validation claims.

motivations.constraint: Bound agent skill context without removing domain meaning or model-owned capability.
motivations.reason: An agent skill reaches a correct result faster when it loads only the current canonical owner while retaining every motive, constraint, proof duty, and judgment input the task needs.
motivations.failure_prevented: A short skill package that saves tokens by making the executor guess, reread, or lose the tools and context needed for the domain result.

Agent skill migration that loses accepted behavior

actors: Agent skill author, executor, reviewer, user, and package owner.
objects: Agent skill package, source skill, build log, contract, task graph, eval case, and receipt.
actions: Create, update, standardize, import, validate, evaluate, reject, restore, and report an agent skill.
states: Agent skill baseline, RED, candidate, accepted, rejected, blocked, restored, and released states.
invariants: An agent skill keeps its domain purpose, accepted behavior, authority, proof, and portability.
variants: Agent skill instructions vary by domain while shared package checks retain one contract.
An agent skill has user or project availability; a derived skill preserves applicable behavior and maintains its own source baseline.
interfaces: Agent skill frontmatter, SKILL.md, support files, Mise task graph, CI, and registry eval interfaces.
authorities: The user controls agent skill purpose changes, destructive migration, publication, and deployment.
failures: A skill package can fail through generic content, lost behavior, weak triggers, stale proof, or host lock-in.
recoveries: Restore the accepted skill package digest, repair the lowest owner, and rerun the Mise task graph.
evidence: Skill package CI, trigger evals, behavior evals, source lineage, semantic review, and restoration receipts.
time: Agent skill sources, web receipts, baselines, and acceptance output must be current for the run.
resources: The Mise task graph measures wall time, CPU, memory, storage, network, cache, context, process, cost, and attention.
quality: An agent skill must improve task success without losing correctness, speed, simplicity, portability, or domain judgment.
terminology: Agent skill is the package; skill body, reference, asset, script, test, Mise task, example, and eval are primitive kinds.
exclusions: The skill package does not invent private domain facts, execute unsupported side effects, publish, or replace task-specific judgment.

research_receipts.claim: Agent skills should start from real expertise, project artifacts, failures, and execution traces instead of generic model knowledge.
research_receipts.limitations: The guidance defines authoring practice but does not specify this skill-factory task graph.

research_receipts.claim: An agent skill uses YAML frontmatter with typed name, description, compatibility, metadata, and allowed-tools fields, followed by Markdown and optional progressively disclosed resources.
research_receipts.limitations: The format specification does not prove domain behavior or require Mise.

research_receipts.claim: YAML mappings require unique keys, so duplicate frontmatter fields cannot be accepted as an unambiguous skill contract.
research_receipts.limitations: The YAML data model does not define Agent Skills field names or domain behavior.

research_receipts.claim: A domain concept scheme distinguishes preferred, alternate, hidden, broader, narrower, and related terms.
research_receipts.limitations: SKOS models knowledge organization, not agent skill execution.

research_receipts.claim: Requirements link stakeholder expectations, rationale, verification, validation, states, timing, and change authority.
research_receipts.limitations: The handbook addresses engineered systems, so skill-factory uses its trace and proof pattern rather than its project process.

research_receipts.claim: Provenance relates entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, and time.
research_receipts.limitations: PROV-O supplies a provenance model, not a complete agent skill receipt schema.

research_receipts.claim: Use-case work should map context, measure outcomes and risks, manage findings, and keep governance cross-cutting.
research_receipts.limitations: The playbook is voluntary risk guidance and does not define agent skill package conformance.

research_receipts.claim: Mise self-update resolves the latest GitHub release without a version argument, supports noninteractive confirmation, and can exclude plugin updates.
research_receipts.limitations: Package-managed Mise builds may disable self-update and require their owning package manager.

research_receipts.claim: The official Mise schema enumerates configuration, task, task-configuration, and tool fields for the installed release.
research_receipts.limitations: Schema presence does not show that a primitive is useful for a particular agent skill or that its domain outcome passes.

research_receipts.claim: Mise tasks can declare dependency edges, bounded parallel execution, source and output freshness, and content-based caching whose correctness depends on complete inputs.
research_receipts.limitations: The task runner can reuse deterministic computation and schedule independent work, but it cannot decide domain meaning or replace live model and human judgment.

disconfirmation.question: Can more domain detail make an agent skill worse?
disconfirmation.result: Yes. The guidance warns that broad or exhaustive instructions can waste context and send execution down irrelevant paths.
disconfirmation.disposition: Bound specificity to facts that alter agent skill behavior, proof, or recovery, and move conditional detail into references.

skill_body.role: Tell an agent how to create or change a skill package without replacing its purpose.
skill_body.outcome: The agent skill body leads an executor to a proved skill package result.
skill_body.motivation: The agent skill body keeps domain judgment visible while package mechanics stay bounded.
skill_body.value: The agent skill body turns a package request into a numbered workflow whose Mise, model, branch, loop, and stop owners produce checkable progress.
skill_body.failure_prevented: An agent skill body that describes packaging without producing the requested domain result.
skill_body.proof: Agent skill workflow tests prove every numbered step names Mise or model work and the full flow contains real branch, loop, return, receipt, and stop behavior.

references.role: Hold skill package contracts that are too conditional for the always-loaded body.
references.outcome: Agent skill references supply the exact conditional rule needed for a correct result.
references.motivation: Skill package references keep the main path short without hiding required rules.
references.value: Agent skill references reduce context cost while resolving a real execution branch.
references.failure_prevented: Skill package references that add reading cost without changing a decision or proof.
references.proof: Every skill package reference has a load trigger and one owning decision.

assets.role: Provide skill package templates and machine-readable policies for deterministic generation.
assets.outcome: Skill package assets give deterministic steps the exact inputs needed for the domain result.
assets.motivation: Skill package assets make generated owners repeatable without pretending seeds are finished work.
assets.value: Skill package assets turn source-backed choices into reusable, checkable inputs.
assets.failure_prevented: Generic skill package assets that pass through without affecting the use-case outcome.
assets.proof: A new agent skill contains the declared owners and remains blocked on seed content.

scripts.role: Implement repeatable agent skill scaffolding, validation, migration planning, and evaluation checks.
scripts.outcome: Agent skill scripts produce deterministic progress and receipts for package operations.
scripts.motivation: Agent skill scripts reduce repeated model work and produce parseable receipts.
scripts.value: Agent skill scripts convert repeatable use-case mechanics into fast, reproducible actions.
scripts.failure_prevented: Agent skill scripts that automate activity without advancing or proving the package outcome.
scripts.proof: The Mise task graph runs script interfaces with tested exits and outputs.

tests.role: Pin user-visible agent skill commands, artifacts, failure branches, and package boundaries.
tests.outcome: Agent skill tests prove the behavior and boundaries the user depends on.
tests.motivation: Agent skill tests prevent factory edits from weakening accepted package behavior.
tests.value: Agent skill tests expose a wrong package path before it reaches a user.
tests.failure_prevented: Skill package tests that assert internals while the user-visible outcome stays broken.
tests.proof: The skill package test task observes RED and then exits 0 after the owner is repaired.

mise_tasks.role: Expose one Mise task graph for every deterministic agent skill job.
mise_tasks.outcome: The Mise task graph moves each skill package operation through one proved dependency path.
mise_tasks.motivation: The Mise task graph keeps local and remote skill package checks on the same dependency path.
mise_tasks.value: The Mise task graph schedules real skill package progress and blocks invalid acceptance.
mise_tasks.failure_prevented: A Mise task graph that runs generic checks but cannot advance the agent skill outcome.
mise_tasks.proof: Task graph tests and skill package CI exit 0.

examples.role: Show complete agent skill runs for creation, update, import, validation, and failure handling.
examples.outcome: Agent skill examples let an executor reproduce a successful or blocked package operation.
examples.motivation: Agent skill examples remove guesses about commands, evidence, and visible output.
examples.value: Agent skill examples shorten the path from trigger to a correct package result.
examples.failure_prevented: Skill package examples that look plausible but omit commands, proof, or recovery.
examples.proof: Each agent skill command and likely failure has one current worked run.

evals.role: Measure agent skill triggering, behavior, failure recovery, speed, and retained purpose.
evals.outcome: Agent skill evals decide whether the package reaches its use-case result under realistic prompts.
evals.motivation: A trigger eval and behavior eval catch packages that look valid yet fail the use case.
evals.value: Agent skill evals turn subjective acceptance into repeatable evidence and bounded judgment.
evals.failure_prevented: Skill package evals that grade package shape while task success regresses.
evals.proof: Fresh agent skill eval cases satisfy saved assertions without protected regressions.

policies.role: Define acceptance, authority, lifecycle, portability, and nonregression rules for an agent skill package.
policies.outcome: Agent skill policies keep every package change inside its intended use-case boundary.
policies.motivation: A skill package needs explicit rules where a valid shape could still permit a wrong result.
policies.value: Agent skill policies turn protected domain behavior into reviewable acceptance conditions.
policies.failure_prevented: A skill package passes its mechanics while violating purpose, authority, or protected behavior.
policies.proof: Each agent skill policy has an owning Mise gate and a current decision receipt.

schemas.role: Define machine-readable shapes for agent skill inputs, outputs, state, and proof.
schemas.outcome: Agent skill schemas make deterministic package boundaries parseable and fail closed.
schemas.motivation: A skill package cannot reliably validate receipts or state when their structures are implicit.
schemas.value: Agent skill schemas expose missing, stale, or malformed evidence before semantic acceptance.
schemas.failure_prevented: A skill package accepts structurally ambiguous state that cannot support its use-case proof.
schemas.proof: Schema-owning agent skill checks reject malformed fixtures and accept current valid records.

records.role: Retain agent skill research, decisions, invocations, lineage, experiments, and lifecycle evidence.
records.outcome: Agent skill records connect each accepted package state to its cause and proof.
records.motivation: A skill package needs durable evidence to distinguish a current result from an unsupported claim.
records.value: Agent skill records support review, restoration, and current acceptance without repeating discovery.
records.failure_prevented: A skill package cannot explain what changed, why it changed, or how to restore it.
records.proof: Record-owning agent skill checks validate freshness, completeness, linkage, and current digests.
